break_rights: military (SCRA) — Active-duty service members with deployment or permanent-change-of-station orders may end a lease under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3955.

domestic violence — A victim of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault or stalking (or a household member who is a victim) may end the lease under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, sections 24-26, with written notice within 3 months of the most recent act and proof such as a protective order or police/medical record.

uninhabitable conditions — A landlord must keep the home up to the State Sanitary Code (105 CMR 410); if serious problems are not fixed after written notice, the tenant may claim constructive eviction and leave.

landlord harassment — Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, section 14 bars a landlord from shutting off utilities or seriously interfering with quiet enjoyment; a forced-out tenant may claim constructive eviction.
early_break_fee: No statewide cap or set fee in statute; if the lease has an early-termination fee you are generally bound by it, and without one you may owe rent for the rest of the term, reduced by any re-renting.
rent_control_note: State law bans local rent control statewide under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 40P; no city, including Boston or Cambridge, has active rent control.
roommate_rules: Co-tenants who both sign are each liable for the full rent, not just their share, and one roommate leaving does not end the lease or the others' duty to pay. Adding or removing a name needs the landlord's written agreement. A tenant cannot evict a roommate; only the landlord can end a tenancy through court.

break_rights: military (SCRA) — Service members entering active duty may end a lease under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3955.

domestic violence — A victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking (or whose child is a victim) may end the lease under Mich. Comp. Laws 554.601b, with at least 30 days' written notice and a protection order, police report or qualified third-party verification.

uninhabitable conditions — The landlord must keep the home fit and in reasonable repair under Mich. Comp. Laws 554.139; if serious problems are not fixed after notice, the tenant may leave and claim constructive eviction.

medical — A tenant who has lived there more than 13 months and becomes unable to live independently, or becomes eligible for subsidized senior housing, may end the lease on 60 days' written notice under Mich. Comp. Laws 554.601a, with a notarized doctor's statement for incapacity.
early_break_fee: No statutory formula or cap; what you owe depends on the lease, but a lease cannot waive the landlord's duty to mitigate damages, and an acceleration clause must state you may not owe the full amount.
rent_control_note: State law bans local rent control under Mich. Comp. Laws 123.411; no Michigan city has rent control.

break_rights: military (SCRA) — Service members entering active duty may end a lease under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3955, with the lease ending 30 days after the next rent due date.

domestic violence — A tenant or authorized occupant who is a victim of domestic abuse, criminal sexual conduct, sexual extortion or harassment and fears imminent violence may end the lease under Minn. Stat. 504B.206, with signed advance written notice and a qualifying document such as an order for protection or law-enforcement report.

uninhabitable conditions — The landlord must keep the home fit for its intended use under Minn. Stat. 504B.161; if serious health or safety problems are not fixed, a court may treat the tenant as constructively evicted, and rent-escrow or abatement remedies under Minn. Stat. 504B.385 may apply.
early_break_fee: No statutory formula or cap in Minn. Stat. ch. 504B; what you owe depends on the lease, so read it for an early-termination clause before leaving.
rent_control_note: No statewide rent cap; local rent control is allowed only if voters approve it at a general election under Minn. Stat. 471.9996, and St. Paul voters did so, limiting increases to 3% in 12 months with exceptions.
roommate_rules: Co-tenants who both sign are each liable for the full rent, not just their share, and one roommate leaving does not end the lease or the others' duty to pay. Adding or removing a name needs the landlord's written agreement. A tenant cannot evict a roommate; only the landlord can end a tenancy through court.

break_rights: military (SCRA) — Service members entering active duty may end a lease under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3955.

uninhabitable conditions — If the landlord materially breaches the lease or its duties to keep the home safe, the tenant may give written notice that the lease will end in at least 14 days if the breach is not fixed, under Miss. Code Ann. 89-8-13; after 30 days' written notice of a defect the tenant may also repair and seek reimbursement under 89-8-15.
early_break_fee: No statute limits or caps early-termination fees; a fee in the lease generally applies, and without one the tenant may still owe rent for the rest of the term.
rent_control_note: No statewide rent control, and state law bars local rent control unless the Legislature first approves it under Miss. Code Ann. 21-17-5; no city has it.
roommate_rules: In most leases tenants are jointly and severally liable, meaning each tenant is responsible for the entire rent, so one roommate leaving does not end the others' duty to pay. Adding or removing a name needs the landlord's written agreement. A tenant cannot evict a roommate; only the landlord can end a tenancy through court.

break_rights: military (SCRA) — Service members entering active duty may end a lease under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3955.

domestic violence — A tenant who is, has been, or is in imminent danger of becoming a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking is not liable for rent after vacating, under Mo. Rev. Stat. 441.920, if notice and documentation are given; the landlord may charge a reasonable termination fee under 441.920.6.

uninhabitable conditions — If the landlord does not fix a code violation after 14 days' written notice, the tenant may repair and deduct under Mo. Rev. Stat. 441.234, and serious unlivable conditions may support a constructive-eviction claim in court.
early_break_fee: No statutory cap or formula; an early-termination fee must be in the lease and must be a reasonable estimate of the landlord's actual loss, not a punishment for leaving.
rent_control_note: No statewide rent control, and state law bans local rent control under Mo. Rev. Stat. 441.043, as amended effective August 28, 2025.
roommate_rules: Co-tenants who both sign are each liable for the full rent, not just their share, and one roommate leaving does not end the lease or the others' duty to pay. Adding or removing a name needs the landlord's written agreement, and assignment needs the landlord's written assent under Mo. Rev. Stat. 441.030. A tenant cannot evict a roommate; only the landlord can end a tenancy through court.

domestic violence — A tenant who is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking by a household member may end the lease under Mont. Code Ann. 70-24-153, with 30 days' written notice and documentation such as a protection order, police report or advocate's letter.

uninhabitable conditions — The landlord must keep the home fit and habitable under the Montana Residential Landlord and Tenant Act; if serious problems are not fixed after notice, the tenant may leave and claim constructive eviction.
early_break_fee: No statutory cap; a fee must be in the lease, and without a legal exit the tenant may owe rent until the landlord re-rents or the lease ends.
rent_control_note: No statewide rent control, and state law bans local rent control under Mont. Code Ann. 7-1-111; no Montana city has rent control.

break_rights: military (SCRA) — Service members entering active duty may end a lease under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3955.

domestic violence — A tenant who is a victim of domestic violence, or whose household member is, may be released under Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-1431.01, with a protection order, restraining order or certification and written notice choosing a release date 14 to 30 days later; rent is owed for the month the lease ends and no fee may be charged for ending it, and other co-tenants stay bound.

uninhabitable conditions — The landlord must keep the home fit under Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-1419; if serious problems are not fixed after notice, the tenant may use the remedies in Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-1425 and 76-1427, including ending the lease, and may claim constructive eviction.
early_break_fee: No statutory cap; a fee must be in the lease, and without a legal exit the tenant may owe rent until the landlord re-rents or the lease ends.
rent_control_note: No statewide rent control, and state law now bans local rent control under 2025 LB 266; no Nebraska city has rent control.
roommate_rules: Co-tenants who both sign are each liable for the full rent, not just their share, and one roommate leaving does not end the lease or the others' duty to pay, including after a domestic-violence release, where other co-tenants stay bound. Adding or removing a name needs the landlord's written agreement. A tenant cannot evict a roommate; only the landlord can end a tenancy through court.

break_rights: military (SCRA) — Service members entering active duty may end a lease under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3955, with no early-termination fee.

domestic violence — A tenant or co-tenant who is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, harassment or stalking may end the lease under Nev. Rev. Stat. 118A.345, with written notice and proof within 90 days of the incident; the lease ends 30 days after notice or at the end of the current rental period, whichever is sooner.

uninhabitable conditions — If the home substantially lacks required habitability items under Nev. Rev. Stat. 118A.290, the tenant must give written notice and the landlord has 14 days to fix it; if not fixed, the tenant may end the lease immediately under Nev. Rev. Stat. 118A.355.
landlord harassment — If the landlord locks the tenant out or intentionally shuts off an essential service, the tenant may end the tenancy and seek damages under Nev. Rev. Stat. 118A.390.
early_break_fee: No statutory cap; leases commonly charge 1 to 2 months' rent as an early-termination fee, and without a legal exit the tenant may owe rent until the landlord re-rents or the lease ends.
rent_control_note: No statewide rent cap and no local rent-control ordinance in force; there is no express statewide preemption statute, so check the local ordinance before relying on a number.
roommate_rules: Co-tenants who both sign are each liable for the full rent, not just their share, and one roommate leaving does not end the lease or the others' duty to pay. Adding or removing a name needs the landlord's written agreement. A tenant cannot evict a roommate; only the landlord can end a tenancy through court.

break_rights: military (SCRA) — Service members may end a lease under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3955, and New Hampshire also has a state military-termination law at N.H. Rev. Stat. 540:11-a.

domestic violence — A tenant may end the lease under N.H. Rev. Stat. 540:11-b, effective January 1, 2025, if the tenant or a household member was a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking within the most recent 150 days, with written notice and verification such as a protective order, police report or professional's letter, and must vacate within 30 days of notice.

uninhabitable conditions — The landlord must provide safe, sanitary housing meeting minimum standards under N.H. Rev. Stat. 48-A:14 and 540-A:3; if serious problems are not fixed after notice, the tenant may claim constructive eviction.
early_break_fee: No statutory cap; a fee must be in the lease, and without a legal exit the tenant may owe rent for the rest of the term.
rent_control_note: No statewide rent control and no municipality has ever enacted rent control; New Hampshire has no preemption statute on the subject.
roommate_rules: If rent is shared, anyone who signs the lease may have to pay the total rent, not just their share, and one roommate leaving does not end the lease or the others' duty to pay. Adding or removing a name needs the landlord's written agreement. A tenant cannot evict a roommate; only the landlord can end a tenancy through court.

break_rights: military (SCRA) — Service members entering active duty may end a lease under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3955.

domestic violence — A tenant who, or whose child, faces an imminent threat of serious physical harm may end the lease under the New Jersey Safe Housing Act, N.J.S.A. 46:8-9.4 to 46:8-9.12, with written notice and a restraining order, law-enforcement record, medical record or domestic-violence specialist certification; the lease ends 30 days after the landlord receives notice.

uninhabitable conditions — The landlord must keep the home livable under the implied warranty of habitability; if serious problems are not fixed after notice, the tenant may leave and claim constructive eviction in court.
landlord harassment — If a landlord's harassing conduct makes the home unlivable, the tenant may claim constructive eviction and end the lease.
medical — A senior tenant moving to a care facility may end the lease 40 days after the landlord receives written notice, under New Jersey law for senior care moves.
early_break_fee: No statutory cap; a lease-break fee must be reasonable and not punitive, and courts often look at whether it is about 1 to 2 months' rent, because the landlord must also try to re-rent.
rent_control_note: No statewide rent cap, but state law allows local rent control and more than 100 towns, including Newark, Jersey City, Hoboken, Paterson, Elizabeth, Trenton and Bayonne, have local ordinances.
roommate_rules: Co-tenants who both sign are each liable for the full rent, not just their share, and one roommate leaving does not end the lease or the others' duty to pay. Adding or removing a name needs the landlord's written agreement. A tenant cannot evict a roommate; only the landlord can end a tenancy through court, and New Jersey landlords generally need good cause to evict under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.
